summary:
We developed PORKONITOR, an autonomous biomedical monitoring web dashboard designed for 180-day deep-space missions. The system connects to a subcutaneous biosensor implanted in each crew member's forearm (BIO-CHIP-X04) to continuously track physical biomarkers—heart rate, bone density, cortisol, sleep, and cumulative radiation—alongside objective mental health metrics including stress, cognitive fatigue, isolation, and homesickness.

Our platform addresses the challenge of safeguarding astronaut health across isolated environments and communication delays through an interactive 180-day mission simulation calibrated with real biomedical datasets from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR). When critical anomalies or Solar Particle Events (SPE) occur, the system triggers color-coded early warnings, highlights affected regions on a 3D holographic body scanner, and provides step-by-step first-aid protocols and preventive countermeasures.

PORKONITOR is essential because it shifts space medicine from reactive to autonomous and preventive, empowering crews to detect and manage physical and psychological risks independently before they jeopardize mission success.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?PORKONITOR is an autonomous biomedical and psychological monitoring web console built for 180-day space missions. The platform is modeled around a subcutaneous biosensor implanted in each astronaut's right forearm (BIO-CHIP-X04) that transmits telemetry via ultra-low-power inductive/MedRadio links to the spacecraft without relying on bulky external wearables. Through an interactive orbital trajectory timeline (Earth–Moon–Earth), the dashboard simulates all 180 mission days. It continuously tracks physical biomarkers (live animated BPM/ECG waveforms, HRV, bone density via calcium/CTX, cortisol, sleep duration, and cumulative radiation) alongside psychological metrics (stress/anxiety, cognitive fatigue, isolation, and homesickness). Whenever critical thresholds are breached, PORKONITOR triggers color-coded alerts, highlights affected regions on a 3D holographic body mesh, and provides step-by-step microgravity first-aid protocols (including AED defibrillator procedures with crew restraints and Solar Particle Event SPE sheltering).

Benefits and intended impact

  • Autonomous deep-space medical care: Eliminates critical delays caused by Earth-space communication latency, empowering non-medical crew members with clear explanations and actionable emergency protocols.
  • Objective mental health tracking: Cross-references involuntary physiological markers (cortisol, HRV, sleep deficit) with behavioral isolation patterns to identify psychological strain early without relying on subjective self-reporting.
  • Preventive health management: Shifts space healthcare from reactive crisis response to continuous prevention, safeguarding crew readiness for long-duration Lunar and Martian missions.

Tools, coding languages, and software used

  • Web Development: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, using Chart.js for dynamic telemetry graphs.
  • Scientific Data: Real biomedical datasets sourced from the NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) (specifically SpaceX Inspiration4 studies OSD-575 and OSD-571) and physiological thresholds from the NASA Human Research Program (HRP).
  • Collaboration & Workflow: Visual Studio Code (using Live Share for real-time team coding) and GitHub.

How is it creative and what factors did our team consider?

  • Creativity: Instead of showing boring medical spreadsheets, we turned health tracking into a visual, intuitive experience: an orbital journey that reveals health issues gradually, a body scanner that highlights exactly where the problem is located, and plain-language explanations so any astronaut can understand their condition without being a doctor.
  • Factors considered: Our team accounted for hardware safety constraints (battery-free inductive power and a 72-hour onboard flash buffer during signal blackouts), the five core hazards of human spaceflight (radiation, isolation, distance, gravity changes, and hostile environments), microgravity ergonomics during medical emergencies, and individualized pre-flight baseline calibration for every crew member.
